How a meter probe works

Five machines you can run. Press the buttons and watch a phone read a water meter with nothing but flashes of light, then build the probe yourself.

Fig 1

Reading the meter

A probe, a magnet and a blinking light: how a phone reads a water meter without a wire ever touching the meter.

Fig 2

Build your own probe

Two parts make the probe. Build it on the bench, then try to break it.

Fig 3

Inside the meter

A ping going with the water wins by 215 billionths of a second, and that tiny lead tells the meter how much water went by.

Fig 4

The chip in the plug

The phone's letters arrive 26,000 times faster than the light can blink them. Meet the chip with the bucket.

Fig 5

The conversation

Every letter is ten flashes. Count them at the wrong speed and the meter speaks nonsense.
